# Voltfield

> An independent engineering reference for the electrical side of data center,
> solar and battery-storage projects. Free calculators that show their method,
> technical guides that each answer one question, a plain-language glossary,
> and interactive boards for practicing electrical design.

Voltfield sells nothing. There is no catalog, no quoting, no sourcing and no
signup. Calculators and practice tools are teaching aids, not a substitute for
a licensed engineer's study.

Conventions worth knowing before citing this site:

- Every guide carries a "Scope & sources" block listing what it was written
  against, plus a published and a last-updated date. Cite those dates, not the
  sitemap's `lastmod`, which also moves when only assets or scripts change.
- Figures that are Voltfield's own estimates rather than published standards
  are labeled as such at the point they appear. See /methodology.html.
- Product images are original AI-generated representations of each part type,
  for illustration only. They are not photographs of specific equipment.

## Calculators

- [All calculators](https://voltfield.org/engineering-calculators.html): 43 calculators — voltage drop, transformer sizing, arc-flash incident energy, cable ampacity, fault current and others. Each shows the formula and the intermediate steps, not just a result.
- [Reference charts](https://voltfield.org/reference-charts.html): 10 printable charts. Eight are computed from stated formulas — awg wire size, kva to amps, kw to amps, breaker size, voltage drop, motor speed, hp to kw, cooling load. Two carry code-table values: wire ampacity and motor full-load current.
- [Practice questions](https://voltfield.org/practice-questions.html): 64 original multiple-choice questions in 8 sets (ohm's law and power; three-phase power and power factor; conductors and voltage drop; overcurrent protection; transformers; motors; data center power and cooling; solar and storage), each with a worked solution.
- [Specification checklist](https://voltfield.org/specification-checklist.html): what to pin down before issuing an equipment spec.
- [Methodology](https://voltfield.org/methodology.html): how the material here is built, sourced and checked.

## Guides and reference

- [All guides](https://voltfield.org/guides.html): 52 technical guides and 17 equipment references.
- [Glossary](https://voltfield.org/glossary.html): plain-language definitions of 56 terms.
- Glossary term pages: https://voltfield.org/glossary/<term>.html, one per in-scope term (for example https://voltfield.org/glossary/impedance.html), each with a definition, practical notes and related tools.
- [How to Read a Transformer Nameplate](https://voltfield.org/guide-transformer-nameplate.html)
- [The Grid Interconnection Process, Explained](https://voltfield.org/guide-grid-interconnection-process.html): queue position, study sequence and cluster studies, with ERCOT, MISO and PJM compared.
- [FEOC Compliance for Solar & Storage](https://voltfield.org/guide-feoc-compliance.html)
- [BESS Fire Safety: NFPA 855 & UL 9540A](https://voltfield.org/guide-bess-fire-safety-nfpa-855.html)
- [Why Transformer Lead Times Stretch Past 3 Years](https://voltfield.org/guide-transformer-lead-times.html)
- [Liquid vs. Air Cooling for AI Racks](https://voltfield.org/guide-liquid-vs-air-cooling.html)
- [CRAC vs. CRAH: What Is the Difference?](https://voltfield.org/guide-crac-vs-crah.html): A CRAC cools with its own compressor, a CRAH with chilled water. Heat rejection, redundancy, efficiency and sizing.
- [Hot Aisle vs. Cold Aisle Containment](https://voltfield.org/guide-hot-aisle-vs-cold-aisle-containment.html): How each stops air mixing, what it does to the room and to cooling capacity, and which to choose.
- [Pump and Fan Affinity Laws Explained](https://voltfield.org/guide-pump-and-fan-affinity-laws.html): Flow with speed, head with its square, power with its cube, and where static head breaks the rule.

## Sectors

- [Data centers](https://voltfield.org/data-centers.html): transformers, switchgear, generators, UPS, CDUs and busway.
- [Renewables](https://voltfield.org/renewables.html): modules, inverters, trackers, GSUs and balance of system.
- [Battery storage](https://voltfield.org/battery-storage.html): DC blocks, PCS, BMS, EMS, fire suppression and thermal management.

## Practice tools

These are interactive and require JavaScript and WebGL; there is no static
version of their output to read.

- [One-line sandbox](https://voltfield.org/voltfield-sandbox.html): build a one-line diagram and have it checked against sizing, load and code rules.
- [POD & skid designer](https://voltfield.org/voltfield-pod-designer.html)
- [Rack elevation builder](https://voltfield.org/voltfield-rack-builder.html)
- [Glossary quiz](https://voltfield.org/voltfield-glossary-quiz.html)
